intro:
BBC Sport reports that Italian side Como have agreed a deal worth around £31m to sign Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah. The move, described by the broadcaster as a transfer agreement valued at more than £30m, represents a notable transaction involving a player from one of England's leading clubs.

The report does not provide further specifics about personal terms or timings in the excerpt, but it makes clear that Como and Chelsea have reached terms on a sizable fee for the defender, according to BBC Sport.

According to BBC Sport, Como have agreed a deal of about £31m to sign Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea. The outlet describes the arrangement as worth more than £30m and identifies the player and the clubs involved. Those are the confirmed facts provided in the report.

sections.text:
Chelsea are a London-based club that compete at the top level of English football and have a long history of developing or signing players who move on in significant transfers. Trevoh Chalobah is identified in the report as a Chelsea defender, and he has been associated with Chelsea's senior setup in recent seasons.

Como are an Italian club that, by virtue of engaging in this kind of transfer, are investing substantially in their squad. Moves between clubs in England and Italy are a regular feature of the European transfer market, and a fee in the region of £30m+ represents a major outlay for many clubs outside the very biggest spenders.
